design_rationale: Allocation was systematic rather than truly randomized ('os 2 primeiros pertenceriam ao Grupo B, os 2 seguintes ao Grupo F e assim sucessivamente...').

domain_judgments.rationale: Baseline demographic variables were similar across groups, but type and invasiveness of surgical procedures across groups were not controlled or adjusted for in the analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ...foram incluídas no estudo, de modo sistemático, ou seja, os 2 primeiros pertenceriam ao Grupo B, os 2 seguintes ao Grupo F e assim sucessivamente, passando pelos Grupos M, S e D até perfazerem um total de 20 pacientes em cada grupo.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were recruited consecutively prior to intervention assignment, so selection into the study was not related to post-intervention outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Após a aprovação pela Comissão de Ética e o consentimento escrito dos pais, 100 crianças, com idades entre 2 e 12 anos, estado físico ASA I, II e III, de ambos os sexos, programadas para procedimentos cirúrgicos ortopédicos de membros inferiores, urogenitais, anais e abdominais infraumbilicais, foram incluídas no estudo...

domain_judgments.rationale: The interventions were clearly defined and administered in a controlled clinical environment during anesthesia induction.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Logo após a indução da anestesia, nos pacientes do grupo B foi realizado bloqueio peridural caudal com bupivacaína a 0,25%... no grupo F, foi realizado bloqueio peridural caudal com fentanil... pacientes do grupo M, receberam morfina... pacientes do grupo S receberam sufentanil... Nos pacientes do grupo D, foi administrado supositório de diclofenaco potássico, por via retal...

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Interventions were administered as intended per protocol, and co-interventions (rescue analgesia) were administered according to predefined thresholds.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A partir deste período, a avaliação era feita pela enfermagem e/ou pais, com base na observação de mudança de comportamento e/ou postura das crianças, tentando relacionar estes dados com a presença de dor e necessidade de complementação com analgésicos.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data appear complete for all 100 participants across the planned 20 patients per group without reported attrition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ...até perfazerem um total de 20 pacientes em cada grupo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (investigators, nurses, and parents) and older children were not blinded to the interventions, which differed visibly in route (caudal block vs. rectal suppository) and drug, potentially influencing subjective pain ratings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A partir deste período, a avaliação era feita pela enfermagem e/ou pais, com base na observação de mudança de comportamento e/ou postura das crianças, tentando relacionar estes dados com a presença de dor e necessidade de complementação com analgésicos.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective clinical trial protocol or registration is available to rule out selective reporting of outcomes and time points.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is moderate according to ROBINS-I guidelines, primarily due to non-blinded assessment of subjective pain outcomes and lack of adjustment for potential confounding surgical factors across systematically allocated groups.

design_rationale: Participants were described as randomly allocated to one of three groups (diclofenac, pethidine, or control).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although patients were randomly allocated and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups, the methods of sequence generation and allocation concealment were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were allocated randomly to receive either diclofenac 1 mg/kg, pethidine 1 mg/kg or no analgesia (control group) after induction of anaesthesia.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was described as double-blind with recovery ward nurses blinded to intraoperative treatment, and administration of rescue analgesia followed an established protocol without non-protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pethidine 1 mg/kg was given intramuscularly in the recovery ward if thought necessary by the recovery nurse, who was not aware which drug, if any, had been given intra-operatively.

domain_judgments.rationale: A large proportion of patient-reported visual analogue pain scores were missing at several time points (e.g. only 12-16% at awakening, 12-40% at 30 min) due to drowsiness or distress related to treatment and pain, and scores at 30 min and 1 h could not be analyzed due to missingness and rescue analgesia.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Very few patients recorded scores immediately after they awoke (Table 3)... Failure to record a score at the observation time occurred on some occasions because children were too sleepy or too distressed to move the cursor.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (nurses) were blinded to treatment allocation, and validated visual analogue instruments were used identically across study arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One of two recovery nurses also assessed the patients' pain with a standard visual analogue scale when they awoke, and 30 minutes and one hour postoperatively... who was not aware which drug, if any, had been given intra-operatively.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered clinical trial protocol or statistical analysis plan is available, and some planned post-operative pain time points were omitted from statistical analysis post hoc.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The pain scores at 30 minutes and one hour postoperatively could not be compared because many of the children required pethidine in the recovery ward.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by substantial missing outcome data for patient-reported pain scores across multiple early postoperative time points due to sedation or distress directly related to the intervention and pain outcomes.

design_rationale: The authors state that sixty children were randomly allocated to one of three treatment groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The method of sequence generation and allocation concealment was not described, and there were baseline differences between groups in age and weight.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: They were allocated randomly to one of three treatment groups to receive intra-operatively either rectal diclofenac 2 mg/kg (group A), intramuscular papaveretum 0.2 mg/kg (group B) or no analgesia (control, group C).

domain_judgments.rationale: While administration occurred under anaesthesia and ward outcome assessors were blinded, ward nurses were not blinded to group allocation (leading to all control children being administered papaveretum within 10 minutes), representing deviations from intended interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 20 children in the group that received no analgesia were given intramuscular papaveretum by the nursing staff at a mean time of 10 minutes (SEM 1.79) after their return to the ward (Table 4). This was administered because the nursing staff considered these children to have marked pain.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 60 enrolled participants (20 in each of the three groups) have complete outcome data reported across all assessment time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 60 children were studied, 20 patients in each treatment group. Demographical data are shown in Table 1.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome assessor was blinded to group allocation and any postoperative rescue analgesia administered, minimizing detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The investigator, who was blind to the group allocation of the patients and to any postoperative analgesia administered, assessed the patients postoperatively with reference to pain, appearance, side effects and respiratory rate.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective trial registration or pre-specified analysis protocol is available, raising some concerns for selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Statistical analysis of the data for pain, appearance and the use of postoperative analgesia was performed using the Chi-squared test with Yates' correction. Between-group comparisons of parametric data were made using Student's unpaired t-test.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to insufficient reporting of random sequence generation and allocation concealment, potential deviations from intended interventions in the unblinded ward setting, and the absence of a pre-registered analysis protocol.

design_rationale: The study states that 60 children were randomly allocated into one of three groups prior to anaesthesia in a randomized double-blind trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: The authors state that children were randomly allocated, but provide no details on sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Children were randomly allocated into one of three groups prior to anaesthesia. Those who were given i.v. nalbuphine, those who were given diclofenac suppositories and a control group who received no analgesia.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention was administered under general anaesthesia, the operator, observer, and recovery staff were blinded, and all randomized patients received their assigned interventions with no reported protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The extractions in all patients were performed by the same experienced blinded operator... Pain related behaviour was evaluated in all patients by the same blinded observer... Recovery staff were unaware of the experimental group the patient was in.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 60 randomized participants (21 nalbuphine, 19 diclofenac, 20 control) were accounted for across all outcome analyses and tables with no missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 60 patients divided into three groups as shown in Table 2 were studied.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment utilized a validated objective pain scale administered consistently across groups by a trained observer blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pain related behaviour was evaluated in all patients by the same blinded observer using an objective pain scale adapted from one previously described by Hannallah and colleagues [14], see Table 1.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered trial protocol is available to confirm that all prespecified analyses and time points were reported without selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Statistical analysis was performed using standard analysis of variance on parametric data and Kruskal-Wallis analysis of variance on the objective pain scores. A P-value of <0.05 was considered significant.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged to have some concerns primarily due to the lack of details regarding random sequence generation and allocation concealment (Domain 1) as well as the absence of a pre-registered trial protocol (Domain 5).

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that participants were randomized in an open randomized trial to receive either rectal diclofenac or intravenous morphine.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study states that children were randomized, but the method of sequence generation and allocation concealment are not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In connection with the preoperative assessment, 3 months before surgery, the children were randomised to receive either diclofenac 1mg/kg given rectally or i.v. morphine 0.05mg/kg as perioperative analgesic treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label, the interventions were administered as single-dose perioperative analgesics under anaesthesia strictly according to protocol, and analyses followed assigned groups without important deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This open randomised study was designed to investigate the analgesic and anti-emetic properties of rectally administered diclofenac compared with opioid (morphine) given i.v. in connection with strabismus surgery in children.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were available for all 50 randomized children (25 per group) for the primary outcomes of vomiting and pain.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The prevalence of postoperative vomiting in the two groups... Diclofenac (n = 25), Morphine (n = 25)

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was open-label without blinding of patients, parents, or staff, which could introduce bias in subjective and patient-/parent-reported outcomes such as nausea and pain, although vomiting itself is relatively objective.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The child, parent or both were contacted by phone the following day to determine the incidence of nausea, vomiting and pain during the first 24h after surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no indication of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan to assess whether selective outcome reporting occurred.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prevalence ratios and confidence intervals were calculated according to standard statistical methods. Analyses were done with software program, SAS Institute Inc. 1999.

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns due to lack of details regarding sequence generation and allocation concealment, lack of blinding in an open-label assessment of partially subjective outcomes, and absence of a pre-registered analysis plan.
